articles.summary: Grants awarded to 412 nonprofits, including 229 in Virginia Funds will support human needs, environmental stewardship, education, and community vitality Foundation giving is funded by Dominion Energy shareholders The Dominion Energy Charitable Foundation recently awarded $4.5 million in grants, funded by shareholders, to nonprofit organizations across multiple states. Grants were awarded to 412 organizations across the Dominion Energy footprint, including 229 in Virginia, which received just over $3.3 million in support. This funding supports programs and services focused on a variety of causes, including hunger relief, dental and health care clinics, housing stability, early literacy, community gardens and nature trails as well as arts and culture. Grant recipients include: Dulles South Food Pantry in Loudoun County, to assist with access to reliable, healthy food Partnership for Housing Affordability in Richmond, for the expansion of its Housing Resource Line The Mariners’ Museum
articles.title: Dominion Energy Charitable Foundation Awards $4.5 million in Grants to Nonprofit Organizations Across Multiple States

articles.summary: CAYCE, S.C. (Nov. 17, 2026) – Dominion Energy customers in Walterboro recently attended a kickoff event for the Neighborhood Energy Efficiency Program (NEEP). They are among the over 1,500 customers in the area who are eligible for free energy-saving products and services through NEEP, which offers home assessments, on-site education and installation of energy-efficient products to income-eligible customers. articles.summary: Filed testimony reflects strong alignment with key conditions proposed by Commission Staff and the Office of the Attorney General Division of Consumer Counsel ensuring robust financial safeguards and independence for Dominion Energy Virginia. Preserves all elements of existing benefits package, including delivering immediate bill relief and long-term affordability through four years of shareholder-funded residential bill credits and continued access to NextEra Energy’s capital, scale and proven ability to buy, build, finance and operate more efficiently. Positions Virginia to meet extraordinary growth in electricity demand while preserving Dominion Energy Virginia's local leadership and full accountability to the Virginia State Corporation Commission. Builds on NextEra Energy’s proven record at Florida Power Light Company, where typical residential bills are 37% below the national average and reliability is more than 60% better than the national average.
